use: Used mid-story to lead into the surprising next event; the sa holds the listener's attention.

example.romaji: soshitara sa, kyuu ni ame ga futte kita no.
example.ja: そしたらさ、急に雨が降ってきたの。
example.english: And then, out of nowhere, it started pouring.

notes: Soshitara also means 'in that case': soshitara, ashita ni shiyou.

kana: いっしゅん〜かとおもった
use: Telling about a brief scare or mix-up; the thing you wrongly thought goes in the gap.

example.romaji: isshun saifu otoshita ka to omotta.
example.ja: 一瞬財布落としたかと思った。
example.english: For a second I thought I'd lost my wallet.

examplePolite.romaji: isshun saifu o otoshita ka to omoimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 一瞬財布を落としたかと思いました。
examplePolite.english: For a moment I thought I'd dropped my wallet.

notes: Isshun alone means 'an instant': isshun de, 'in no time'.

english: ...and that's the story; I hear that...
use: Wraps up a story with its point, or passes on something you heard.

example.romaji: de, kekkyoku saifu wa ie ni atta tte hanashi.
example.ja: で、結局財布は家にあったって話。
example.english: So the wallet was at home the whole time. That's the story.

examplePolite.romaji: kekkyoku, saifu wa ie ni atta tte hanashi desu.
examplePolite.ja: 結局、財布は家にあったって話です。
examplePolite.english: In the end, the wallet was at home all along.

notes: As hearsay: raigetsu kekkon suru tte hanashi da yo, 'I hear they're marrying next month'.

kana: じかんたつのはやいね
polite: jikan ga tatsu no wa hayai desu ne
politeJa: 時間が経つのは早いですね
use: Said when you notice how long it's been, like meeting an old friend or seeing a child grown up.

example.romaji: mou ichinen? jikan tatsu no hayai ne.
example.ja: もう一年？時間経つの早いね。
example.english: A year already? Time flies, huh.

examplePolite.romaji: mou ichinen desu ka. jikan ga tatsu no wa hayai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: もう一年ですか。時間が経つのは早いですね。
examplePolite.english: A year already. Time really flies.

notes: Tatsu here is 'pass' (time), a different word from tatsu 'stand' with the same sound.

kana: ことしもあとすこしだね
romaji: kotoshi mo ato sukoshi da ne
polite: kotoshi mo ato sukoshi desu ne
politeJa: 今年もあと少しですね
use: Standard December small talk at work, in shops and with neighbours.

example.romaji: kotoshi mo ato sukoshi da ne. hayakatta naa.
example.ja: 今年もあと少しだね。早かったなあ。
example.english: The year's almost over. That went fast.

examplePolite.romaji: kotoshi mo ato sukoshi desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今年もあと少しですね。
examplePolite.english: The year's nearly over, isn't it.

notes: Often paired with yoi otoshi o, 'have a good new year', said before the year ends.

kana: おしょうがつはかえるの？
use: Asked in December, since many people go back to their parents' home for the New Year holidays.

example.romaji: oshougatsu wa kaeru no? jikka doko dakke?
example.ja: お正月は帰るの？実家どこだっけ？
example.english: Going home for New Year? Where's your family from again?

examplePolite.romaji: oshougatsu wa jikka ni kaerimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: お正月は実家に帰りますか？
examplePolite.english: Are you going back to your family home for New Year?

notes: Kaeru here means going back to your hometown; jikka is your parents' home.

src: 早く週末にならないかな
ja: 早く週末にならないかな
kana: はやくしゅうまつにならないかな
use: A half-joking mid-week grumble to friends or coworkers, or to yourself.

example.romaji: mada suiyoubi ka. hayaku shuumatsu ni naranai kana.
example.ja: まだ水曜日か。早く週末にならないかな。
example.english: Only Wednesday? I can't wait for the weekend.

notes: Works for any day or event: hayaku natsuyasumi ni naranai kana.
